confirmed.title: Trace eval chip bands 1–5 LLM-judge scores on a 0..1 scale — failing evals always render a green 'success' chip
confirmed.description: evalTone() bands the node eval aggregate with 0..1 thresholds (>=0.7 success, >=0.4 warning), and the local comment claims the score is '(0..1)'. But the LLM-judge aggregate is a weighted mean of 1–5 dimension scores (backend/app/services/eval.py compute_aggregate_score, toxicity inverted as 6-x; RunDetailView.tsx:413 correctly renders it as `${evalAggregate.toFixed(2)} / 5`, and AlertsCard's eval_avg hint says '1–5'). The minimum possible LLM-judge aggregate is 1.0, which is >= 0.7, so every LLM-judge eval chip on the run trace — including a worst-case 1.0/5 that fails the threshold — shows the green success tone. This inverts the design system's core 'eval pass/fail band' chroma semantics on the primary trace surface. Only deterministic evals (0/1 exact/regex/schema aggregates) band correctly.
confirmed.fix: Band by the value's actual scale: `const tone = score > 1 ? (score >= 3.5 ? "success" : score >= 2.5 ? "warning" : "destructive") : (score >= 0.7 ? ...)`, and append the scale to the chip copy (`eval 3.40/5`) and title so the number is self-describing. Update the evalAggregate() doc comment.

verdict.note: Confirmed. evalTone() at TraceNodeRow.tsx:101-105 bands aggregate_score with 0..1 thresholds (>=0.7 success, >=0.4 warning), but every aggregate the backend produces is on a 1-5 scale: backend/app/services/eval.py compute_aggregate_score() is a weighted mean of 1-5 dimension scores (toxicity inverted as 6-x), and — stronger than the finding claims — deterministic evals too: eval_deterministic.py _score_dict() maps match_score to `1.0 + match_score * 4.0` and json_schema/numeric return 5.0 or 1.0. So the minimum possible aggregate is 1.0 >= 0.7, and EVERY eval chip on the trace (including a worst-case failing 1.00/5) renders the green success tone; the destructive/warning branches are dead code. The finding's one inaccuracy is its caveat that deterministic 0/1 aggregates band correctly — they don't (a failing deterministic eval yields 1.0, also green), which makes the bug worse, not better. Other surfaces confirm the 1-5 scale: RunDetailView.tsx:413 renders `${evalAggregate.toFixed(2)} / 5` and EvalScoresChart divides by 5. The chip also prints `eval 1.00` with no scale suffix, which reads as a perfect score on a 0-1 scale next to a green chip. This is misleading status chroma (a failed eval presented as success) on the primary trace surface and directly inverts the design system's eval pass/fail band semantics — P0 per 'actively misleading UI'. Proposed fix direction (band on the 1-5 scale, add '/5' to copy/title, fix the '(0..1)' doc comment at line 92) is correct, though the score>1 heuristic can be simplified since all aggregates are 1-5.

confirmed.title: Button focus ring never renders: Tailwind v4-only `ring-3` in a v3 build
confirmed.description: The project runs Tailwind v3.4.19 (package.json / node_modules), but Button's base classes use v4-only `ring-3`. Compiling a probe against the project's own tailwind.config.ts emits NO CSS for `ring-3` (while `ring-2` compiles), so `focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50` produces no ring at all — `ring-ring/50` only sets a color variable that nothing consumes. The only surviving focus affordance is `focus-visible:border-ring`, a 1px border tint that is ~1.4:1 contrast against the default bone (dark) / ink (light) primary button fill — effectively invisible keyboard focus on the app's most common interactive element, in BOTH themes. `aria-invalid:ring-3` and `aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20` are dead for the same reason. This silently violates the system's 'interactive elements need visible focus (focus-ring)' bar everywhere Button is used.
confirmed.evidence: focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50 ... aria-invalid:border-destructive aria-invalid:ring-3
confirmed.fix: Replace `ring-3` with `ring-2` (both occurrences in the cva base string), or apply the house `.focus-ring` utility from globals.css (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--bg), 0 0 0 4px var(--ring)`), which is what the rest of the app uses.

verdict.note: Confirmed by compiling a probe against the project's tailwind.config.ts (Tailwind v3.4.19): `ring-3` emits no CSS while `ring-2` does, and `ring-ring/50` only sets --tw-ring-color which nothing consumes without a width utility. tailwind.config.ts does not extend ringWidth. No mitigation exists: globals.css even has a global `:focus-visible { outline: none; }` (line 255), and the house `.focus-ring` box-shadow utility (line 354) is opt-in and not applied by Button. Remaining focus affordance is only `focus-visible:border-ring`, a 1px border tint with very low contrast against the primary fill in both themes (dark: ring #c8bfb2 vs primary #ece6dc; light: #756d62 vs #312d27). `aria-invalid:ring-3` is equally dead. Effectively invisible keyboard focus on the most-used interactive primitive = blocking a11y failure, P0. Fix: replace both `ring-3` occurrences with `ring-2`, or apply the `.focus-ring` utility.

confirmed.title: Schedule trigger preview labeled "Next runs (UTC)" renders local-time values
confirmed.description: The trigger node's cron preview heading says "Next runs (UTC)" (line 352) and the hint says "Standard 5-field cron (UTC)" (line 345), but each timestamp is rendered with new Date(runAt).toLocaleString(), which converts to the browser's local timezone. The backend genuinely returns UTC instants (backend/app/services/cron_utils.py: `itr.get_next(datetime).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)`, serialized via isoformat in api/meta.py), so for any user not in UTC the values shown under the UTC label are wrong per that label — a user verifying `0 9 * * 1-5` in IST sees "2:30:00 pm" under "Next runs (UTC)". Line 362 ("Last scheduled run: {new Date(lastFiredAt).toLocaleString()}") has the same raw-formatting problem. These timestamps are also plain sans text — the design system requires all timestamps in font-mono + tabular-nums.
confirmed.evidence: • {new Date(runAt).toLocaleString()}
confirmed.fix: Make label and value agree: either format in UTC — new Date(runAt).toLocaleString(undefined, { timeZone: "UTC", timeZoneName: "short" }) — or relabel the block "Next runs (local time)". Wrap the list items and the "Last scheduled run" value in font-mono tabular-nums (or reuse formatFullTimestamp with an explicit UTC variant in lib/format-date.ts).

verdict.note: Verified end-to-end. Backend returns tz-aware UTC instants: cron_utils.py:16 does `.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` and meta.py serializes via `dt.isoformat()` (e.g. "...T09:00:00+00:00"). Frontend NodeInspector.tsx renders each with `new Date(runAt).toLocaleString()` (line 355) under the heading "Next runs (UTC)" (line 352) and hint "Standard 5-field cron (UTC)" (line 345), so any non-UTC user sees browser-local times presented as UTC — e.g. IST user checking `0 9 * * 1-5` sees 2:30 pm labeled UTC. This is misleading info on the scheduling config surface and can lead users to "correct" their cron to the wrong offset, so P0 (rubric: misleading, wrong info presented as current) is justified. Line 362 "Last scheduled run" has the same raw toLocaleString formatting. No mitigation found elsewhere (no shared UTC formatter used here). Secondary, correct-as-claimed: the timestamps are plain text-xs sans, violating the font-mono + tabular-nums rule for timestamps (that alone would be P1). Proposed fix (format in UTC with timeZoneName, or relabel to local time, plus mono/tabular) is sound.

confirmed.title: Observability view switcher is a role="tablist" whose children are not tabs
confirmed.description: The Triage | Trust | Sessions | Cost & usage switcher wraps FilterChip components in role="tablist", but FilterChip (src/components/ui/filter-chip.tsx:12-15) renders a plain <button> with aria-pressed and no role="tab", aria-selected, or aria-controls. ARIA requires tablist children to be role="tab"; screen readers will announce an empty/broken tab list, and none of the tablist keyboard conventions (arrow-key navigation) exist. The same FilterChips are correctly wrapped in role="group" in TriageStream.tsx:56, so this one surface has invalid semantics. Properly built tablists exist elsewhere (CanvasSidebar.tsx:102-122, WorkflowCanvas.tsx:2465-2496), proving the intended pattern.
confirmed.evidence:
<div className="flex items-center gap-1.5" role="tablist" aria-label="Observability view">
      <FilterChip
        label="Triage"
confirmed.fix: Change role="tablist" to role="group" (matching TriageStream.tsx:56), since FilterChip already exposes aria-pressed toggle state; or, if tab semantics are wanted, add role="tab"/aria-selected/aria-controls props to FilterChip and wire arrow-key handling.

verdict.note: Verified. frontend/src/app/observability/page.tsx:456 has role="tablist" aria-label="Observability view" wrapping four FilterChip components; FilterChip (src/components/ui/filter-chip.tsx) renders a plain <button> with aria-pressed and no role="tab"/aria-selected/aria-controls, and no arrow-key handling exists. This violates the ARIA tablist pattern (tablist children must be tabs), so screen readers will announce an empty/malformed tab list with conflicting toggle-button semantics inside it. The identical chips are correctly wrapped in role="group" in TriageStream.tsx:56, confirming this is drift, not intent. Not P0: the buttons remain focusable, clickable, and labeled, so the control is degraded rather than inaccessible. P1 is right. Proposed fix (swap to role="group") is correct and minimal.

confirmed.description: The Label primitive (src/components/ui/label.tsx) is a plain sibling <label>, so without htmlFor + a matching control id there is no programmatic association: screen readers announce the Input/Textarea/Select with no name, and clicking the label doesn't focus the field. confirmed.title: Run/severity status→tone map re-implemented 8+ times and already drifted (running = warning vs active vs muted)
confirmed.description: lib/run-status.ts is the canonical status→variant map (running/pending/queued → warning, awaiting_approval → accent), but at least eight components re-implement their own map and the semantics have drifted: lib/run-status.ts:3-17 (runStatusVariant: running→warning), components/observability/run-row.tsx:16-22 (statusDotClass: running→bg-warning, awaiting_approval→bg-accent), components/observability/SessionsView.tsx:60-66 (StatusMix inline: only failed/cancelled/completed colored, so a RUNNING session count renders text-muted), components/observability/ViolationBreakdown.tsx:30-34 (statusTone), app/observability/page.tsx:254-265 (kindClass: awaiting→text-accent), components/runs/TraceNodeRow.tsx:43-51 (statusRing: running→ring-warning) and 108-114 (guardrailTone), components/canvas/run/RunDeck.tsx:283-299 (statusClass: running/awaiting_approval→text-active, a different token than everywhere else) and 325 (eventClass), components/canvas/run/RunNodeResultCard.tsx:38-46 (statusTone: running→border-active). The same run status gets amber on /observability, 'active' hue on the canvas RunDeck, and plain muted in SessionsView — a direct violation of 'chroma reserved for data semantics' being consistent.
confirmed.evidence:
status === "failed" || status === "cancelled"
  ? "text-destructive"
  : status === "completed"
    ? "text-success"
    : "text-muted"
confirmed.fix: Extend lib/run-status.ts with the missing projections — runStatusTextClass(status), runStatusDotClass(status), guardrailTone(status) — and replace the local maps in SessionsView, run-row, ViolationBreakdown, TraceNodeRow, RunDeck, RunNodeResultCard, and observability/page.tsx with imports, deciding once whether live statuses are 'warning' or 'active'.

verdict.note: Verified all cited maps. lib/run-status.ts (runStatusVariant) is the canonical map: running/pending/queued -> warning, awaiting_approval -> accent. At least seven other files re-implement local status->tone maps and the semantics have already drifted: run-row.tsx:16-22 (running -> bg-warning, matches lib), TraceNodeRow.tsx statusRing (running -> ring-warning), but RunDeck.tsx statusClass maps running AND awaiting_approval -> text-active (a different token than warning/accent), RunNodeResultCard.tsx statusTone maps running/awaiting_approval -> border-active, and SessionsView.tsx StatusMix (lines 60-66) only colors failed/cancelled/completed, so a running or awaiting_approval count in a session renders text-muted. Net effect confirmed: the same "running" run status is amber on /observability, active-hued on the canvas run deck, and plain muted in SessionsView; awaiting_approval is accent in some places and active in others. Even if text-active was an intentional token introduced with the run lens, it was not reconciled with the canonical map, which is exactly the drift. This matches the P1 rubric line "duplicated ad-hoc component logic that has already drifted" and violates chroma-reserved-for-data-semantics consistency. Proposed fix (centralize projections in lib/run-status.ts and decide once between warning vs active for live statuses) is sound. Files: frontend/src/lib/run-status.ts, frontend/src/components/observability/SessionsView.tsx, run-row.tsx, ViolationBreakdown.tsx, frontend/src/app/observability/page.tsx, frontend/src/components/runs/TraceNodeRow.tsx, frontend/src/components/canvas/run/RunDeck.tsx, RunNodeResultCard.tsx.

confirmed.title: Millisecond/latency formatter implemented 7 times with 4+ visibly different output formats, including on the same screen

verdict.note: Verified all seven cited implementations exist exactly as claimed. src/lib/format.ts exports only pluralize and formatCostUsd — no shared ms formatter. Line 132 renders `<span className="block truncate">` inside a td of a `w-full border-collapse` auto-layout table (line 83) with no table-fixed or max-w-0 anywhere; wrapper at line 80 is overflow-x-auto. With table-layout:auto, the nowrap from `truncate` makes the cell's min content width the full text width, so ellipsis can never trigger — long names widen the table and horizontally scroll the numeric columns out of view. Proposed fix (w-full max-w-0 on name cell, or table-fixed with column widths) is the standard remedy.

Even with equal-width labels, the centers of ticks 1 and 3 sit ±(labelWidth/4) (~6–10px) away from their gridlines, and unequal widths ('0ms' vs '1.2s' vs '5s') drift further — on a component whose whole purpose is positional accuracy of spans on a shared axis.

verdict.note: Confirmed. Line 122 lays out the 5 tick labels with `flex justify-between` while the gridlines they annotate are absolutely positioned at left:(i/4)*100% (lines 147-153) inside a container with the identical horizontal extent (left-10 right-[4.5rem] vs ml-10 mr-[4.5rem]). Proposed fix (absolute-position each label at the same i/GRID_STEPS geometry with -translate-x-1/2, endpoints anchored) is sound.
